notes: Original narrative and full practice retained. Open slots: senza, grazie, and supported receptive bridge uses of uscire (planned productive chapter 10) and mostrare (planned productive chapter 12). No production item requires those early verbs; their later plan dates remain unchanged.

Contractions and full stressed con noi belong to the current preposition bundle. No clitic, demonstrative, embedded question under sapere, new past tense or audio. All listed reference forms require actual prose demonstrations; do not assume generic licensing certifies them.

Ada authorizes carrying her sealed envelope and its pickup is explicit. Elena never opens it. Marco’s recognition is stated as remembering the envelope; no contents or old-project history is revealed. The original library tool remains in Paolo’s blue box, separate from Marco’s workshop tools.

Delivered wrong-shop, first-landmark, authorized-envelope-transfer, accompanied/unaccompanied, corrected-route and workshop aids support the first-use stages. The route is fictional, anchored to the library door facing the square; shop front faces the square, workshop front faces the stop. Three inline scenes plus cover, one vignette and one diagram stay within the course caps. The prior-coverage warning includes new joined preposition spellings built from known articles; reviewer should assess actual load and support.

First sinistra/destra/davanti now have an immediate library-facing direction diagram at s005c; first dietro has an immediate window/books plane contrast at s005d, before the full corrected route. Cast accompaniment is a vignette of the actual volunteers. Two precise spatial diagrams remain within the configured cap.

segments.text: Il foglio è sul tavolo del bar. La foto è su un foglio, non nel libro blu. Ada legge il nome Marco. «La bottega di Marco è in centro, vicino al ponte. Dove è Marco oggi? Non so. Ma la sua bottega è qui.» Ada guarda la piazza fuori dalla finestra. Elena prende la foto con il foglio; Paolo prende la penna.

Ha la scatola, ma non ha il libro blu della biblioteca.

grammar.title: Grammatica
grammar.rule: a + il → al; da + la → dalla; in + il → nel; su + gli → sugli; di + la → della.
grammar.note_en:
A preposition links a person, object or action to another part of the sentence: going to a destination, coming from somewhere, being in a place, or doing something with someone. Italian choices do not map one-for-one onto English “to”, “at” and “in”. Learn the actual combinations: andiamo in centro means “we go to the town centre”, vado in biblioteca means “I go to the library”, and andiamo alla bottega means “we go to the workshop”. A can locate or direct: alla fermata is “at/to the bus stop”, according to its verb. In can likewise occur with movement or position. It is not a rule that a always means movement and in always means rest.

When a, da, in, su and di meet a definite article, their written forms join. These are articulated prepositions: a + il becomes al, a + la becomes alla; da + il becomes dal and da + la becomes dalla; in + il becomes nel and in + la becomes nella. Compare sul from su + il and sulla from su + la. We already know di as “of”: di + il becomes del, while di + la becomes della. The reference table pairs the combinations with actual nouns from the story. The noun determines its article; the preposition contributes its relation. Thus la bottega gives nella bottega (“in the workshop”), and il negozio gives nel negozio (“in the shop”).

Before a vowel, the article l’ remains visible within the joined form: nell’autobus is “in the bus”, dall’autobus is “from/out of the bus”, dell’autobus is “of the bus”. The apostrophe marks the elision; it is not a possessive mark borrowed from English. Sugli scaffali combines su with gli, the plural article already met before scaffali, and means “on the shelves”. Sul tavolo means “on the table”; sulla sedia means “on the chair”. The initial photo su un foglio, “on a sheet”, keeps the indefinite article separate.

Da also goes with a person’s name to mean going to that person or their premises: andiamo da Marco means “we go to Marco’s place”. It is not andiamo a Marco. Dal bar, “from the bar”, instead identifies an origin. Con means “with”: con noi is “with us”. The form noi stays the same after con; it is a full, stressed pronoun here, not an unstressed object clitic. Senza means “without”: the two volunteers leave senza Ada. When Marco says non parlo della busta senza Ada, he means “I do not talk about the envelope without Ada present”. Here parlare di describes a topic, rather than ownership.

Tra and fra both mean “between/among” in the displayed position examples. There is no left-versus-right distinction between them. A sinistra and a destra mean “on/to the left” and “on/to the right”. Davanti al negozio means “in front of the shop”; dietro il negozio means “behind the shop”. Vicino al ponte means “near the bridge”. In la bottega è vicina alla fermata (“the workshop is near the stop”), vicina is an adjective agreeing with feminine bottega; in lavora vicino al ponte (“works near the bridge”), vicino describes location without that agreement.

Andare, “go”, has irregular present forms: vado/vai/va/andiamo/andate/vanno, “I go / you go / goes / we go / you go / they go”. Formal Lei uses va, as in Lei va con noi? (“Are you coming with us?”). The new reading also meets esce/escono (“goes/go out”) and mostra (“shows”), with their actual meaning aids; the production questions practise the preposition patterns rather than require a new verb paradigm. Directions are tied to the people’s orientation and landmarks. The wrong shop and the workshop are distinct places, so the corrected route changes where the volunteers actually arrive.
